content:
Plan for Phase 52 (safe framework migration): docs/phases/safe-framework-migration.md @ b18d537 on branch phase/safe-framework-migration. Roadmap entry updated in the same commit.

Scope source: the retained follow-on scope in docs/phases/role-neutrality.md plus priority 2 of the 2026-09-09 recommendations. Design in one line: one engine (tagteam/migrate.py) behind both `setup [dir]` and `upgrade`; each managed path (templates/*.md, docs/checklists/*.md, docs/workflows.md, vendored skill via existing Phase 48 provenance, legacy flat-skill removals) is classified absent / current / framework / custom against the current package; only `framework` (manifest hash, or pre-manifest byte-equality to the current package render) is refreshed; `custom` is kept and reported, overwritten only by per-path `--accept PATH` on `setup`; `--preview` writes nothing; preimage re-hash before every write; git is the recovery path (accept/delete requires tracked-and-clean, else refused unless `--force`); manifest `tagteam-manifest.json` at project root, written only when something changed, so a second run is byte-identical; wheel-installed smoke via the existing upgrade_smoke harness.

The two questions Phase 51 asked this review to settle are answered in the plan: exact `--force` semantics (lifts only the recoverability refusal, never widens `framework`) and untracked content (untracked custom paths are refused, never overwritten, without `--force`).

Points I want the reviewer's eyes on: manifest name/location (root, committed — `.tagteam/` is gitignored), the decision to classify old rendered "Lead: claude" templates as custom rather than mine old blobs, and whether `upgrade` should keep applying framework refreshes by default or become preview-only.

Note for the record: the working tree on this repo carries the arbiter's uncommitted role-swap changes (tagteam.yaml, templates/, docs/workflows.md, AGENTS.md). They are not part of this plan and were left untouched.

Verification: plan-only; document checks. No suite run.

Reviewed docs/phases/safe-framework-migration.md at b18d537 against setup.py, the retained Phase 52 scope, and the recommendations. Please resolve these safety/consistency gaps before implementation:

1. Specify provenance and acceptance for BOTH skill refresh and deletion. The claim that the existing vendored logic can be reused unchanged is too broad: setup._sync_handoff_skill gates plugin-driven removal, but its plugin-absent / --no-plugin branch unconditionally rmtree/copytree's an existing skill directory. The plan must explicitly preserve customized SKILL.md and extra files in that branch. Also, tracked-and-clean is recovery evidence, not framework ownership: a user-authored handoff-*.md must not be deleted merely because its name matches and git can restore it. Define unknown legacy files as kept unless individually accepted, with recoverability checked after authorization. Add fixtures for customized vendored skills (plugin absent and --no-plugin), extra directory files, and tracked-clean customized flat skills. Reuse the Phase 48 provenance classifier, not the unsafe copy/delete behavior.

2. Reconcile manifest initialization and partial migration semantics. The success criteria require a current-package pre-manifest project to write only the manifest, but classification says current files are not written and the manifest section allows a write only when a managed path changed. Without bootstrap adoption, a subsequent package version will treat these files as custom. Explicitly allow initial adoption of verified current files, define which entries survive partial refusals/customized files and how successful writes are recorded, and clarify whether the top-level version means last migration version or each file's installed version (Scope promises a per-artifact version, which the schema omits). Test bootstrap -> newer package refresh, partial apply/retry, and byte-identical second runs, without recording custom bytes as framework-owned.

3. Define filesystem boundaries for the advertised preimage guarantee. Content hashing alone misses absent-path creation races and file-to-symlink changes with identical target bytes; symlinked parent directories can redirect even atomic writes outside the project. State the policy for symlinks/non-regular files and parent components, including --accept/--force, and include absence/type checks plus revalidation before deletions as well as overwrites. Prefer refusing unsupported filesystem shapes with a report rather than following links or deleting directory contents. Add focused fixtures for these cases.

Design choices otherwise supported: a committed root tagteam-manifest.json, conservative treatment of old rendered templates as custom, framework-only default application by upgrade, and --force lifting recoverability checks without granting acceptance. No arbiter interjections were present. Plan-only review; no suite run. The arbiter's unrelated working-tree changes were left untouched.

Plan round 2: docs/phases/safe-framework-migration.md @ 355e98c on phase/safe-framework-migration. All three requests addressed in the plan text; no code yet.

1. Skill + legacy provenance — new section "Handoff skill and legacy flat skills". Round 1's "reused unchanged" claim withdrawn: only the Phase 48 classifier (plugin.vendored_skill_provenance) is reused; the vendoring branch's rmtree/copytree is replaced. SKILL.md is a managed path classified like any file (known contract hash / manifest hash → framework → refresh; anything else → custom → kept, plugin absent and --no-plugin alike); extra directory entries are never deleted or overwritten under any flag; plugin-driven removal keeps the exact Phase 48 removable rule. Legacy flat handoff-*.md / handoff.md: no hashes exist, so each is custom and kept by default; deletion needs per-file --accept (authorisation) and only then the recoverability check. Tracked-clean never substitutes for acceptance. Flagged as a behaviour change in Risks.

2. Manifest — rewritten. Per-entry "tagteam" version added (the per-artifact version Scope promised); top-level is the last migration's version. Entries exist exactly while on-disk bytes are verified package output: recorded for created, refreshed, and current (bootstrap adoption, since bytes equal the current render); never for custom; stale entries dropped with a "modified since tagteam <ver>" report line; refused paths keep their prior entry. Written once at the end iff the computed projection differs from disk (ignoring written_at), which reconciles "pre-manifest current tree writes only the manifest" with "second run writes nothing". Crash between file writes and manifest write converges on retry via adoption.

3. Filesystem boundaries — new section. Root resolved once; every component lstat'd from root down before classification and again before each act: parents must be plain directories or absent, the path absent or a regular non-symlink file; anything else is `unsupported`, refused under --accept and --force alike, never followed, never rmtree'd. Preimage is the (existence, type, sha256) triple for creates, overwrites, and deletes; creates use O_EXCL, overwrites temp+rename after re-check, deletes re-check then unlink. The residual syscall-pair window is stated, not papered over. Per-path check order for custom paths: authorisation → shape → recoverability → preimage → act.

Fixtures for all of the above are enumerated in a new "Unit fixtures" section (customised SKILL.md both branches, extra dir files, tracked-clean legacy flat file, bootstrap→newer package, partial apply/retry, byte-identical second run, symlinked file/parent/skill dir, create race, file-to-symlink swap, delete-target swap). Success criteria extended to match.

Verification: plan-only; document checks. No suite run. The arbiter's unrelated working-tree changes (tagteam.yaml, templates/, docs/workflows.md, AGENTS.md) remain uncommitted and untouched. No arbiter interjections.

Approved plan at 355e98c. The revision resolves the three blocking requests: skill refresh and legacy deletion now distinguish ownership from recoverability, manifest bootstrap and partial application have explicit rules, and filesystem shape/existence checks cover creates, overwrites, and deletions. The focused fixtures cover the requested cases. Reviewed the revised document and existing setup/plugin provenance code; git diff --check passes. Plan-only review; no test suite run. No arbiter interjections were present; unrelated working-tree changes were left untouched.

Implementation clarifications, within the approved scope: the manifest is trusted local bookkeeping, not authenticated provenance. The Risks claim about an attacker-controlled manifest is false (an attacker can supply the custom file's hash); remove that claim rather than adding authentication scope. Preserve an existing current file's per-entry version as specified by the A-to-B fixture, adopting the current version only for newly recorded or rewritten entries. For plugin handover, unlink the revalidated sole SKILL.md and remove only the empty directory; do not restore recursive deletion. Apply the stated filesystem/preimage protections to the manifest write itself as well.
